title: Transformers through nanoGPT
summary: Walk through a famous tiny GPT in six files — starting with data, not math. No install, no GPU, just plain-English steps beside the real code.
intro: Language models look mysterious until you see the pipeline: text becomes numbers, numbers go through a network, training adjusts the network, sampling turns numbers back into text.

nanoGPT is the smallest serious version of that story — the repo people actually read when they want to understand GPT-style models. Here it is already translated into short steps you can click through in the browser.
Take it one lesson at a time. Stay on Overview until a step feels familiar; switch to Logic when you want every branch and formula.
learn: How a Shakespeare file becomes a trainable stream of character ids.
What a GPT module is doing when it scores the next character.
What happens in a single training step (loss in, updated weights out).
How sampling turns scores into readable text.
How the README's small Shakespeare run is wired up.
Where "config" files actually plug into the training script.

steps.title: Text to numbers
steps.lesson: Download Tiny Shakespeare and save it the way the trainer expects — one character, one id.
objectives: See where Tiny Shakespeare lives on disk after this script runs.
Understand why one character maps to one integer id here.
Name the files train.py will open later.
steps.primer: No training yet — just housekeeping: download, encode, write binaries.
steps.takeaway: Training data is not "text files"; it is packed integers plus a small codec.
checks: What is stored in train.bin versus meta.pkl?
Why build stoi and itos before writing bytes?

steps.title: The GPT
steps.lesson: The network itself: embeddings, attention blocks, and a guess for the next token.
objectives: Follow one token id from embedding to next-token scores.
See where attention blocks sit in the stack.
steps.primer: This is the densest lesson. Stay on Overview and take one block at a time.
steps.takeaway: A GPT here is embeddings, repeated blocks, and a shared table that both reads tokens and writes scores.
checks: Where do logits get compared to the next id?

steps.title: One training step
steps.lesson: Pull a batch of ids, measure how wrong the guesses are, and update the weights once.
objectives: Trace one optimizer step from batch to weight update.
See where loss is computed and backprop starts.
Notice what gets saved as a checkpoint.
steps.primer: Imagine the binaries from lesson 1 feeding this loop — you are only reading one pass.
steps.takeaway: Training is repeated: sample windows, predict next ids, nudge weights, occasionally save.
checks: What does gradient accumulation change about batch size?
When does the learning rate schedule matter?

steps.title: Text out the other side
steps.lesson: Load a checkpoint and print new Shakespeare-ish lines.
objectives: Load weights and run the model in eval mode.
See how temperature and top_k change randomness.
Watch ids decode back to characters.
steps.primer: You are running the model backwards — from prompt ids to printed text.
steps.takeaway: Sampling reuses the same codec as training; each new id is fed back as context.
checks: Why divide by temperature before softmax?
What happens after each sampled id?

steps.title: The small run
steps.lesson: The cozy settings: a 6-layer model, 256 characters of context, character vocabulary.
objectives: List the hyperparameters that shrink GPT-2 defaults.
See how a README command names this file.
steps.primer: A config file is just variable assignments — no magic syntax.
steps.takeaway: The small run is mostly smaller width, depth, and context plus the char dataset path.
checks: Which settings make this "character Shakespeare" instead of GPT-2 scale?
Where is the dataset path set?

steps.title: How a config lands
steps.lesson: The tiny script that copies those settings into train.py when you run the README command.
objectives: See how a config file executes into train.py globals.
Understand why this is exec, not import.
steps.primer: Short file, big payoff — this is how experiments swap without editing train.py.
steps.takeaway: Running with a config path replaces defaults by executing Python in train's namespace.
checks: What happens when you pass config/train_shakespeare_char.py?
How could a --key=value flag override one variable?

platform.name: Yamori Learn
platform.audience: Curious beginners who learn best by reading real code
prerequisites: You can skim Python without running it.
You do not need PyTorch, a GPU, or prior transformer coursework.

studyGuide.title: Read in Overview first
studyGuide.body: Each file opens in Overview: short blocks in plain language. Stay there until the story makes sense.

studyGuide.title: Click to connect story and source
studyGuide.body: Select a numbered block (or a line of Python). The other pane lights up so you always know where the idea lives.

studyGuide.title: Use Logic when you want depth
studyGuide.body: Logic adds branches, shapes, and math — same file, more steps. Toggle any time; nothing is hidden.

studyGuide.title: Follow the lessons in order
studyGuide.body: The path is deliberate: data, model, training, sampling, then how the small Shakespeare run is configured.
